key_insight: AutoScaffold turns a language model’s training experience into adaptive AI-generated guidance that improves reinforcement learning while requiring no scaffolds at evaluation.
engineering_relevance: The framework offers a reusable way to guide RL training across mathematical reasoning, interactive tasks, search-based QA, and GPU kernel generation.
method: A frozen teacher periodically reviews student training experience and diagnoses bottlenecks.
The teacher generates task-class strategies and hints for individual hard tasks, adapting support as the student improves.
Train the student with scaffolds, then remove them for evaluation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports gains over corresponding RL baselines across four domains; in math, the student surpasses QuestA’s reported accuracy using approximately one-third as many student training steps.
watch_item: Teacher review adds inference overhead, so fewer student training steps do not necessarily imply lower total training cost.
paper_title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
